bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the stated priority: net debt of ₹8,299 crore at 30 Jun 2026, reduced by ₹2,223 crore in the quarter "majorly driven by Cash flow from Operations", against gross debt of ₹28,291 crore ($2.99 bn) and cash and cash equivalents of ₹19,992 crore.
- Deck sets forward leverage targets: VEDL net debt/EBITDA <0.3x near term and <1x medium term (Vedanta Resources target shown as >1x/2x bands in the same chart).
- ROCE of c.29% is presented as evidence of "disciplined capital allocation" (ROCE defined as EBIT net of tax outflow divided by average capital employed).
- Debt is 62% INR and 38% USD/foreign currency; long-term debt of $2.79 bn is sourced 41% Term Loan Fx, 35% Bonds INR, 24% Term Loan INR and 0.1% Bonds Fx, with $1.12 bn at standalone and $1.67 bn at subsidiaries.
- Cash is invested under a Board-approved investment policy in high-quality debt instruments — mutual funds, bonds and bank fixed deposits.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Self-described as "a leading global producer of metals, critical minerals and technology, that powers the industries of today and incubating the industries of tomorrow", with operations across India, Africa, the Middle East and East Asia.
- Post-demerger portfolio (as it exists at end-Q1 FY2027) comprises Zinc India (HZL, 60.71% held), Zinc International (Skorpion 100%; BMM & Gamsberg 74%), FACOR (99.99%), Sterlite Copper (a division, including Nicomet), Vedanta Copper International/Fujairah Gold, VGCB ports, Avanstrate, plus Vedanta Semiconductors and Vedanta Displays. Vedanta Resources Ltd holds 54.72% of Vedanta Ltd through its subsidiaries.
- Deck claims a net debt/EBITDA of 0.30x is "best-in-class in the industry", shown against a peer bar set (Global Peer 1/2, Indian Peer 1/2, industry average, source Bloomberg).
- Credit standing presented as a structural asset: VEDL rated AA+/Stable/A1+ by both ICRA and CRISIL ("highest rating since 2014"); India Ratings at AA-/Watch Developing.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] The demerger was effective 1 May 2026, with four new entities listed on NSE and BSE on 15 June 2026; the deck claims combined market cap of all demerger resulting companies grew by over ₹71,000 crore in Q1 and that this is "unlocking significant shareholder value".
- [Reporting basis] All figures in the presentation and press release cover continuing operations only (the demerged Vedanta as constituted at end-Q1 FY27) and the deck warns they "may not be directly comparable with Vedanta Limited's reported financial statements" prepared under Ind AS 105; EBITDA margin is stated to exclude the copper business.
- [Parent] Vedanta Resources Limited deleveraged by $1.1 billion at group level in Q1 and tied up $1.75 bn of international bonds (avg. coupon 7.4%, avg. maturity 8.5 years) and $2.25 bn of syndicated term loan (~6.4%, avg. maturity 3 years); VRL is rated S&P BB, Fitch BB/Stable and Moody's Ba3/Positive, described as decadal-high ratings, with ICL fully repaid, average maturity >4.5 years and interest cost to be <7.5%.
- [Geopolitical] The closure of the Strait of Hormuz cut Copper Rod sales at Fujairah by 51% YoY, with the deck noting "geopolitical tensions affected supply in whole region".
- [Sensitivities] Annual EBITDA sensitivities disclosed: zinc +$100/MT = ~₹1,000-1,050 crore; lead +$100/MT = ~₹175-200 crore; silver +$1/oz = ~₹200-225 crore; copper +$1,000/MT = ~₹55-70 crore; ₹1 INR depreciation = ~₹350-375 crore.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Vedanta Limited as a post-demerger, zinc-and-critical-minerals-led "leading global producer of metals, critical minerals and technology" with operations across India, Africa, the Middle East and East Asia, run on a low-cost, low-leverage (0.3x net debt/EBITDA) balance sheet.
